title: Application of unmanned aerial system structure from motion point cloud detected tree heights and stem diameters to model missing stem diameters
author: Swayze, Tinkham

steps.title: Generate 10 cm canopy height model
steps.instruction: Create a canopy height model (CHM) with 10 cm spatial resolution from the UAV‑derived point cloud.

steps.title: Detect tree tops and extract heights
steps.instruction: Run the ForestTools localMaximumVariableWindow function on the 10 cm CHM, using a moving‑window search that adjusts the window radius to 0.1 × local‑maximum‑pixel height; retain only detections taller than 1.37 m; the function returns x‑y coordinates of each tree and its estimated height in metres.

steps.title: Extract DBH measurements using TreeLS
steps.instruction: Process the normalized point cloud with the TreeLS package through five sequential operations to obtain stem locations and diameters.

substeps.instruction: Filter point cloud to keep only points between 0.1 m and 4.0 m above ground, discarding all lower and higher points.

Apply the treeMap function: perform a Hough‑transform circle search on a 2‑D slice of the cloud between 1.32 m and 1.42 m, requiring a minimum point density of 0.001 points m⁻² and a maximum possible stem diameter of 1 m; this yields candidate stem centre coordinates and radii.
Run treePoints to crop all points within a 0.5 m radius of each candidate centre and assign a unique tree ID to each cropped set.

Use stemPoints to filter outliers: apply a Hough‑transform noise filter with a maximum stem diameter of 1.5 m and a minimum point density of 0.1 points m⁻²; fit circles to points in successive 0.5 m vertical segments and discard points that lie too far from the fitted circles.

Estimate DBH with tlsInventory: extract a 0.1 m‑thick slice centred at 1.37 m, set the height of all extracted points to 1.37 m, rasterize the slice, and fit a circle using least‑squares estimation with a random‑sample‑consensus algorithm; output each tree’s x‑y location and stem radius in centimetres.
